Working directory for this whole task: D:\CSYE 7370\csye-7270-course\fall-2026\jingyao-y\assignment-7\walker-downfall (the repository; it is the Godot project root). Use Git Bash syntax for shell commands, and cd into that directory first.

Tool rules (these stand in for the course's `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools "Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep,Bash(./scripts/run-test.sh:*),Bash(godot --headless --path godot --import:*),Bash(git status:*),Bash(git diff:*),Bash(git log:*),Bash(ls:*),Bash(mkdir:*)" --disallowedTools "Edit(godot/shaders/**)" --max-turns 60`, plus one addition the user approved for this step; obey them strictly):
- Read, Edit, Write, Glob, Grep are allowed. The Read tool can show PNG images; use it to look at the sheet and your cut parts. Never edit anything under shaders/, and never edit scripts/run-test.sh.
- Bash is allowed ONLY for: `./scripts/run-test.sh ...`; the import command `"/d/CSYE 7370/Godot_v4.7.2-stable_win64_console.exe" --headless --path . --import` (the local equivalent of `godot --headless --path godot --import`; run it after adding new PNGs so they get .import files); `python -I tools/a7_cut_rig_parts.py` (the addition: only this exact script, which you write); `git status`, `git diff`, `git log`, `ls`, `mkdir`. Nothing else: no other python, no other Godot invocations, no git add/commit/stash/checkout.
- Grep/ripgrep skips many game files because .gitignore ignores `/*`; Read files directly by path when Grep finds nothing.
- Stop within about 60 tool calls. If you run out, say exactly what is done and not done.

Context you need beyond the prompt (from CHANGE-BRIEF.md, read it in full): the combat sheet is 64x64 cells, 16 columns x 5 rows, rows = ["south","southwest","west","northwest","north"] (godot_assets/lappland_animator_3d.gd:39), so row west = row index 2; ACTIONS.wave = [10, 3] (columns 10-12). The game's sprite scale is PIXEL_SIZE 0.06 world units per texel for operators (lappland_animator_3d.gd), so a 96x96 viewport at pixel_size 0.06 matches her sprite; use billboard enabled, texture_filter nearest, alpha_cut discard like the operator sprite. Phase table: 30 fps, step 1/30; startup frames 0-5, active 6-9, recovery 10-19, length 20 frames = 0.6667 s; keys on every rig track at f0 (0.0), f6 (0.2), f10 (0.3333), f20 (0.6667); ease-in transitions into frame 6 (accelerating), sweep across active, ease-out settle through recovery; Body:position leans back in startup, lunges on frame 6, returns in recovery; RESET holds the rest pose; loop_mode = Animation.LOOP_NONE for wave_release. The rig's AnimationPlayer callback_mode_process is ANIMATION_CALLBACK_MODE_PROCESS_MANUAL (the brief's clock rule). Billboard.visible and Rig.scale.x must NOT be keyed (the state machine owns them, brief "Authority"); Billboard starts hidden (visible = false). In the cut script, keep pixels unchanged (no recolouring, no palette or colour-count reduction); cut by rectangles/masks only.

The task prompt follows verbatim (from prompts/prompt-4.txt):

---
Read CLAUDE.md first. The rig is res://animations/lappland_wave_rig.tscn,
and its route is keyed cutout. The phase table for wave_release is in
CHANGE-BRIEF.md, in frames at 30 fps.

Build the rig as the brief describes: WaveRig (Node3D) with a Billboard
(Sprite3D drawing the Viewport's ViewportTexture at the game's sprite
scale) and a Viewport (SubViewport, 96x96, transparent) holding Rig
(Node2D) -> Body (Sprite2D), ArmBack (Node2D pivot) -> BladeBack
(Sprite2D), ArmFront (Node2D pivot) -> BladeFront (Sprite2D), and an
AnimationPlayer child of WaveRig with root_node ../Viewport/Rig. Cut the
parts from the brief's cell of godot_assets/lappland_combat_64.png (row
west, column 10) with a committed tool script, tools/a7_cut_rig_parts.py,
into animations/lappland_rig/. Do not edit the sheet.

For a keyed cutout rig: write the wave_release clip (and RESET) for the
AnimationPlayer in that scene, using Godot 4 Animation properties for the
version in CLAUDE.md (loop_mode, not loop). Put a key at every phase
boundary in the table, and list each key's time beside the frame it
comes from.

Add a read-back test, tests/test_wave_rig_readback.gd, that asserts every
track resolves to a real node and property, bone or blend shape (reuse
track_problems in tests/a7_readback.gd, branched on track type); that the
key times and clip length match the brief, compared with a tolerance;
that step is one frame period at 30 fps; and that the loop mode is as
stated.

Run it through ./scripts/run-test.sh and show the real output. Do not
wire the clip into the state machine yet: do not change entities/,
godot_assets/ or any other existing script. Do not commit.
---

When done, reply with: every file you created or changed; the table of each key (track, frame, time, value, transition); the real output of the final test run (pass/fail lines and exit code); and anything you could not do or confirm. Do not report work you did not do.

input.message:
The rig scene, the `wave_release` and `RESET` clips, the cut script and the read-back test are all written. The final run of `./scripts/run-test.sh test_wave_rig_readback.gd 60` passed every check, exit code 0. Nothing is committed. Nothing in `entities/`, `godot_assets/`, `shaders/`, `scripts/` or any other existing script was changed (`git diff --stat` is empty). The sheet was only read.

## Files created (no existing file changed)
- `D:\CSYE 7370\csye-7270-course\fall-2026\jingyao-y\assignment-7\walker-downfall\tools\a7_cut_rig_parts.py`
  - Uses only the Python standard library (zlib and struct, no PIL), so it runs under `python -I`.
  - Reads cell row 2 (west), column 10, at sheet pixel (640, 128). It prints the cell as text, each part's pixel count and bounding box, and a pixel-count check (cell 507 = parts 507, "match").
  - Pixels are copied unchanged or left transparent; parts are cut by rectangles only.
  - Masks in cell coordinates: front blade (15,32)-(24,38); back blade (45,40)-(56,44) plus (42,39)-(46,40); everything else is the body. Pivots (the hands): front (24,37), back (42,39).
- Cut parts, each 64x64 RGBA in cell coordinates, in `D:\CSYE 7370\csye-7270-course\fall-2026\jingyao-y\assignment-7\walker-downfall\animations\lappland_rig\`:
  - `body.png` (466 px), `blade_front.png` (18 px), `blade_back.png` (23 px).
  - Their `.import` files came from the headless `--import` run.
- `D:\CSYE 7370\csye-7270-course\fall-2026\jingyao-y\assignment-7\walker-downfall\animations\lappland_wave_rig.tscn`
  - Tree: `WaveRig` (Node3D) → `Billboard` (Sprite3D) and `Viewport` (SubViewport) → `Rig` (Node2D) → `Body`, `ArmBack` → `BladeBack`, `ArmFront` → `BladeFront`; plus `AnimationPlayer` as a child of `WaveRig`.
  - `Billboard`: shows the viewport through a local-to-scene ViewportTexture; `pixel_size` 0.06, billboard on, nearest filter, alpha cut discard, `visible = false`, y = 0.31. The 0.31 is the operator sprite's own offset, 32·0.06·0.5 − 0.65.
  - `Viewport`: 96x96, transparent, update always, 3D off.
  - `Rig`: at (48,48) so `scale.x` flips her around the centre; nearest filter.
  - Parts: `centered = false`, placed at minus their pivot so they line up with the cell. `ArmBack` has `z_index = -1` so the back blade draws behind the body.
  - `AnimationPlayer`: `root_node = ../Viewport/Rig`, `callback_mode_process = 2` (manual), no autoplay, library `""` holding `RESET` and `wave_release`.
  - `wave_release`: length 0.666667, `loop_mode = 0` (LOOP_NONE), step 0.0333333. `RESET`: length 0.001, one key at t=0 per track, holding the rest pose.
- `D:\CSYE 7370\csye-7270-course\fall-2026\jingyao-y\assignment-7\walker-downfall\tests\test_wave_rig_readback.gd`, which checks:
  - The scene structure and the Billboard and Viewport settings.
  - `Readback.track_problems` from `tests/a7_readback.gd` (reused unchanged; it branches on track type).
  - No track writes `Rig.scale` or the `Billboard`, and every track targets a rig part.
  - `step` = 1/30 within 1e-5; length = 20/30 within half a frame and within 1e-5; LOOP_NONE.
  - Each track has 4 keys at frames 0/6/10/20, within half a frame (1/60 s).
  - The rotation tracks ease in from f0 and ease out from f10.
  - The f0 and f20 values equal `RESET`, and equal the rest values in the scene.
  - The manual clock: process frames do not move the clip, and 6 × `advance(1/30)` puts it at 0.2.
- `logs/test_wave_rig_readback_60fps.log` was written by the test wrapper.

## Key table for `wave_release`
Times: f0 = 0.0, f6 = 0.2, f10 = 0.333333, f20 = 0.666667. A transition of 2 eases in (accelerating into the next key), 1 is linear, and 0.4 or 0.5 eases out. Rotations are in radians; positive is clockwise on screen. Positions are in viewport pixels relative to `Rig`.

| Track | f0 (0.0) | f6 (0.2) | f10 (0.333333) | f20 (0.666667) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Body:position | (-32,-32), tr 2 | (-30,-31) lean back, tr 0.4 | (-35,-32) lunge, tr 0.5 | (-32,-32), tr 1 |
| ArmBack:position | (10,7), tr 2 | (12,8), tr 0.4 | (7,7), tr 0.5 | (10,7), tr 1 |
| ArmBack:rotation | 0.0, tr 2 | -0.7 wound back, tr 1 | 1.4 swept, tr 0.5 | 0.0, tr 1 |
| ArmFront:position | (-8,5), tr 2 | (-6,6), tr 0.4 | (-11,5), tr 0.5 | (-8,5), tr 1 |
| ArmFront:rotation | 0.0, tr 2 | 0.9 wound back, tr 1 | -0.8 swept, tr 0.5 | 0.0, tr 1 |

`RESET` holds the f0 values: Body (-32,-32), ArmBack (10,7) / 0.0, ArmFront (-8,5) / 0.0.

## Could not do or confirm
- **Sheet size:** the sheet is 896x320, which is 14 columns × 5 rows, not the 16 columns the brief says. Column 10 of row west exists and is the cell that was cut.
- **Body lean and lunge:** with keys only at the four boundaries, the body cannot both lean back during startup and be lunged at frame 6. I put the maximum lean on the f6 key. The lunge runs from f6 to f10 with an ease-out (tr 0.4), so most of it lands just after frame 6. Arms follow the same pattern: fully wound back at f6, past the front at f10.
- **Extra tracks:** I added `ArmBack:position` and `ArmFront:position`, which carry the same lean and lunge offsets as the body. The arms are siblings of `Body`, not its children, so without these the blades would come off the hands during the lunge.
- **Front/back assignment:** which blade is front and which is back is my reading of the text dump. The front blade is the one held out ahead of her, to the west; the back blade trails behind, to the east.
- **Not seen moving:** the pivots, angles and whether the motion reads were not checked visually. A headless run draws nothing, so this needs the windowed frame strip.
- **ViewportTexture at runtime:** the test confirms the texture points at `Viewport`, but not that it renders correctly in the game.
- **Not done, per the prompt:** the clip is not wired into the state machine, and nothing was committed.
